a.text: I rarely prayed when I was in Laterano.
This is not to say that my faith was flawed then, or that I was more arrogant or lazier than I am now. Nor can I prove that I am more devout, humble or diligent now.
Because of the environment, though, there were many things that I thought were not necessary when I was in Laterano.
In Laterano, all that the people sought was right there. The Holy City's blessing was right there.

steps.text: 'Lord, I seek your forgiveness...'
'I swore to welcome all who asked for help, treat all of them with equal kindness, and help them to the best of my ability.'
'But I did not keep my word.'
'I can no longer answer the calls for help. I cannot ask them to stay, for we are short on supplies and cannot afford it.'
'I must choose between one group and another.'
'Choose, yes, I have made many choices.'
'But choosing is wrong. And I cannot bear any more wrongs.'
'I cannot go back on my faith, abandon one to save another, save the many and condemn the few.'
'Laterano... my absent home...'
'Why is Laterano the only home?'
'If betraying the high guidance is the path to what I believe in; if only by accepting the heathen can obstacles be truly cleared...'
'...All will be revealed soon.'
'My Lord, forgive my sins... if you truly exist.'

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Who's there?!
Come, now, there's no need for violence.
I've been looking for you, Most Reverend Abbot.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Food is in short supply these days. I hope you don't mind.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Not that minding would do any good. At least it fills the stomach, even if the taste is nothing to write home about.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I don't need to eat right now.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Eat. Don't let it go to waste.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Gerald, leader of Sarkaz. You knew the two Liberi children.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Are you always so direct?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Don't call me a leader. I've seen the true King of Sarkaz. A humble hunter is not worthy of the title.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why do you call yourself a hunter?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Because that's what I am. I hunt to feed myself and others.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I think you have an idea of what's going on here, even though you just arrived today.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Not the full picture.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You lead the group of Sarkaz that lives here. You were latecomers, but at one point you got along well with each other.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Yes. At one point.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Now, conflict has arisen, and it is likely to escalate, given the circumstances.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Yeah, which is why we're leaving.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Normally, you would have the advantage in conflict with the other inhabitants.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: There are few able combatants amongst them, which is one of the reasons they took you in.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But Laterano's intervention has taken away your martial advantage. Leaving is the logical choice.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: You're good with those logical conclusions.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: But I learned a long time ago—

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Our lives are not logical—and I get reminders about that all the time.
The candlelight flickers.
The aging Sarkaz casts his gaze on the wall. The shadows reflected upon it have become blurred, one fading into another.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: We didn't choose to leave because we couldn't live anymore.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Before I came here, I never thought we would have a life like this.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: There were dangers, there was conflict, but we were accepted, we built our own homes, worked for our daily bread...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: That all might seem normal to you, but it was beyond our wildest dreams.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What is the true reason you chose to leave?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: It's simple.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: We see the writing on the wall, just like you do. The rift can no longer be repaired. All that's left is to watch things get worse.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Today it's just an argument, an accusation, but what about tomorrow?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Violent confrontation between the natives and the Sarkaz is likely.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Today's fire was a warning.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Leave now, and we remain friends to be missed.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: But if we allow ourselves to be burdened by attachment and fail to make a decision...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: We will become the Sarkaz that the rest of the world knows—a band of vagabonds who bring conflict with them wherever they go, who are not welcome anywhere, who have no place to call home, and no place to go.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That's just prejudice.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: To us, it's a fact.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: The Sankta have Laterano.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: But where do the Sarkaz belong to?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: It's time.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: It may take a while for the little ones to get used to life without a roof over their heads, but it'll happen.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: As for those two children...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You knew them.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: ...I know a little about where they came from.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The people at the abbey and Raimund don't.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Very few do.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I guess they're wanderers who came from the outside. Their family could be dead, or they could have abandoned their children.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Stefano has taken in other wanderers before, but this place could hardly accommodate any more inhabitants these days.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: But someone secretly took the children in.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You know who it was.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Few secrets can truly be kept forever, especially now, when every single grain counts.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Hyman took them in. She set aside a part of her own rations each day, and stole from the hunted game a few times. I covered it up for her when I discovered it.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Even then, life isn't easy for them.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Where is she now?

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: That's what I'm wondering. She should have come back with game today, but I haven't heard from her.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: She's missing. We don't know where she is.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Whatever happened, I hope she doesn't do anything stupid.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Missing? No, this isn't right.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Hyman would not allow the children to go out, in order to keep their existence a secret. Erendel and Estara's appearance at the sacrarium was not an accident.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Someone brought them outside.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Where is Hyman's home? I want to see it for myself.
The battered wooden hut was a shelter in the storm for the young children.
Abandoned by adults who lacked the means to raised them, they wandered the wastelands and were picked up by a Sarkaz on death's door.
The battered hut was leaky and cold, but there were clean clothes, even if a little tattered, and food, even if the taste was not great.
The walls did a poor job of keeping the cold out. They could gather all the fabric in the house and wear the thickest winter clothes they had, and they would still shiver at night.
But it was home. Mamma was there.
That was where the children felt safe.
The unexpected visitors do not disturb their soft breathing.
They remain slow and steady.
A twisted shadow is cast over the children.

steps.name: Twisted Monster
steps.text: (Incomprehensible whisper))

steps.name: Twisted Monster
steps.text: Hungry... eat...

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Mm...

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: (Rolls over)

steps.name: Twisted Monster
steps.text: Eat, eat...

steps.name: Twisted Monster
steps.text: Cold...
The misshapen monster murmurs incomprehensibly.
The stationary shadow begins to move.
In the moonlight, the monster's powerful tail reaches forward. It brushes the children's soft cheeks, leaving behind a wet scent, then—
It falls into the soft, meek little 'prison.'
Still sleeping soundly, Estara and Erendel instinctively lean towards the comforting scent.

steps.name: Twisted Monster
steps.text: Cold...

steps.name: Erendel
steps.text: Zzz... zzz...

steps.name: Estara
steps.text: Mamma...

steps.name: 'Twisted Monster'
steps.text: Oh... hungry... eat, eat... cold...

steps.name: 'Twisted Monster'
steps.text: Cover... cover...

steps.name: 'Twisted Monster'
steps.text: Cold... cover...

steps.name: 'Twisted Monster'
steps.text: Eren... Sara...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: What have you done, Your Excellency?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: It is improper to eavesdrop on a confession, Reverend Executor.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Oh, don't get me wrong, I wasn't listening to your confession.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Of course, you also know that's not what I'm talking about. Nor am I asking who you sent to ring the bell, how you plan meals for the monastery...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I'm asking about the smell coming from the sacrarium up there.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: You can tell by the smell...? Is the Griffin Arsenal still in business?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: As far as I know, it still supplies practice equipment for various educational institutions.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Including firebombs.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: ...Only the Holy City endures.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I feel your pain. If only Federico learned subtlety and discretion, right?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Still, it's just a corner of a building. It's far from over. Everyone can return to Laterano safely. What do you think?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: You're talking to the wrong man.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I taught everyone how to dismantle the abbey's old weapons and make use of them. Fuel is short, while the winter is long.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: But if you think I instigated the fire... I won't argue.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Come now, don't talk like that. Why don't we sit down and have a chat? Find a solution that we can all accept?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Chat? Solution? Ha.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Is there a solution that doesn't involve turning my back on a human being? I already explained my convictions. Would you truly accept a compromise?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: A group of refugees sought sanctuary at the monastery seven years ago during a great drought. I closed the doors to them.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: They stumbled, almost crawling, back to the wastes. It wasn't the first time I saw a sight like that.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: But I swore before the Lord that it would be the last.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Am I wrong in my convictions, Executor?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: No, of course you're right. I understand your pain.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: There are limits to Laterano's power.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: The laws are imperfect.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I think, and therefore, I doubt.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: For all its imperfections, though, Laterano is good enough for me. I don't want to see her peace and harmony to be threatened by anyone or anything.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I'm sure you can understand that.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: It would be easier for me to persuade my colleagues if we reach an agreement here, and if you refrain from causing any complications.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: My mission would be easier if none of you lifted a finger.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Just because not everyone can go back to Laterano, doesn't mean that no one should.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Laterano is to you as this place is to me.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: There is no need for any further talk between us.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I ask you to leave me to my confession.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Raimund? It's getting late. You should get some rest.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: ...Clément.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I just had something to do.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I'm really sorry about today...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Don't think too much about it. We're leaving anyway.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: ...Right.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: When is that...?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Depends on Gerald. We'll be leaving tomorrow morning, no matter what.

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Probably after Matins.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Matins...

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: Oh! Do you know where Fortuna and Delfina are?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: I was going to... well, I was looking for them.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Did... Gerald not tell you?

steps.name: Raimund
steps.text: What? What are you talking about?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Delfina... she's gone.

steps.name: 'Twisted Monster'
steps.text: Good... bye...
Was that a word of farewell? Or am I mistaken?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You possess basic language skills. It seems my previous assessment was incorrect.

steps.name: 'Twisted Monster'
steps.text: You... are...

steps.name: 'Twisted Monster'
steps.text: Sank... ta.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Indicating a certain level of sapience and cognitive thinking.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Communication appears possible, despite deviation of physical form.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Unknown level of contagion. Unclear if movement patterns change over time. Unknown level of danger.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Notarial Hall regulations permit elimination of potential threats of unknown danger level in order to safeguard the rights of the citizenry.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No sign of resistance. No apparent will to survive.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I'll try to make this quick and painless.
The monster stands in place.
The path before it is blocked. It cannot go back to the past behind.
Justification, anger, pain, all consumed within the no-longer-human body, before it can manifest itself on the hardened hide.
Before an obstacle it cannot surmount, the monster loses the strength to fight, but cannot let go of its last bit of pride.
It stands, silent.
Like a statue.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Executor, no!

steps.name: 'Twisted Monster'
steps.text: Ge..rald...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Hyman... I had half a mind to start praying like Stefano, praying that the monster the Executor was talking about wasn't you.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It was the logical hypothesis. It has now been confirmed.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Move aside, Gerald.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You're interfering with official business.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I know. You can point your gun at me, pull the trigger, bump off a Sarkaz criminal. You won't get any complaints from me.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: But I can't let you kill Hyman.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: ...Explain.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: I can't give you a 'correct' or 'proper' explanation.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: All I can say is—

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Look behind Hyman. There are two children sleeping beyond that door.

steps.name: Hyman
steps.text: Children...

steps.name: Hyman
steps.text: My, children...

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: They have no idea what happened. They're full of hope that you will find their mother.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: They trust you.
The Sarkaz's rough, weathered hand presses against that of a Sankta.
There is no brotherly intimacy, no trust or understanding between friends.
But the Sarkaz's hand presses the Sankta's.
The muzzle of the gun drops, inch by inch.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Don't do it, Executor.

steps.name: Gerald
steps.text: Don't do it, unless you've reached a conclusion that you're satisfied with.
